Return to Bill to view financial data stored on this device.
YOUR FINANCES STAY ON THIS DEVICE.
Bill declares no Internet permission. It does not upload notification text, screenshots, accounts, balances, or ledger data to a Bill server.
Three separate local tools, never one black-box permission

Notifications, read-only payment-result pages, and one-shot screenshots are separate opt-ins. The tile captures the current screen only after your tap. Its OCR is a development experiment that has not passed the privacy release audit, never proves a payment provider, and never posts without your confirmation.

Ledger data stays on this device. You can use the Quick Settings tile for one offline screenshot, or share PNG/text and select a small text file for review. Dedicated Alipay, WeChat Pay, and bank capture still requires real redacted samples.
Each route is separate. This build does not ask you to enable a high-sensitivity permission before it has a verified use.

Not available yet: this build has no verified provider template, so Bill’s listener catalog is empty and it does not read notification text. When a verified route opens, Android Settings > Notification access is where you will enable only that route.
Current status: no verified notification template. Bill is not reading notification text.

Not available yet: the separate observer has no active target app and no screen-text access. A verified source rule, energy test, and a separate opt-in are required before it can observe a result page. When available, Android Settings > Accessibility is the only place to enable it. It never clicks, scrolls, or screenshots.

Experimental on Android 11+: enable the dedicated accessibility service below, then add “Capture receipt” to Quick Settings. Each tap captures the current screen once and creates an on-device review item. It reads no nodes, performs no clicks, and never watches in the background. Its current OCR runtime has not passed the privacy release audit, so it is not a supported payment source. Android blocks secure windows; normal PNG sharing remains the fallback. The system picker needs no whole-library permission.
